title: Unified SDK secret strategies: ephemeral SSO flows, staged API key rotation, and streaming reauth patterns
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: SDK users (Python/TS/Go) need safe, consistent guidance and built-in helpers for handling API keys, staged rotations, enterprise SSO tokens, and streaming session reauthentication. Current patterns across our SDKs are inconsistent which causes security/usability issues: env-vars used unsafely in examples, lack of first-class helpers for dual-key rotations, and fragile streaming reconnects when tokens expire.

Goal: Ship a cross-language SDK pattern + helpers that: 1) make short-lived credentials first-class (ephemeral API keys + SSO token exchange), 2) support staged key rotation (dual-key accept/rollover windows) with simple client helpers, 3) provide streaming-friendly reauth semantics that work with server control-frames and client-side retry/backoff policies, and 4) document secure secret storage guidance for production and local/dev flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Example implementations and ergonomics for Python, TypeScript, and Go included in SDK repos.
2) A small helper library (or core API surface) that exposes: exchangeEphemeralToken(), startManagedRotation(primaryKey, secondaryKey), streamingClientWithReauthHooks().
3) Documentation updated: best practices for secret storage, rotation runbook, and SSO ephemeral token exchange.
4) Automated unit tests that simulate token expiry and validate reconnect + reauth behavior.
5) Security review completed and sign-off obtained before merging.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach: 
- Auth primitives: Add a thin auth module in each SDK that centralizes fetch/refresh logic. Keep public surface minimal: SDK clients accept an AuthProvider object (or factory) which the SDK uses to obtain tokens. Provide built-in implementations: StaticApiKeyProvider, DualKeyRotatingProvider, SsoEphemeralProvider.
- Rotation strategy: Recommend a staged rotation: create secondary key, configure servers to accept both keys for N days, rotate clients to start using secondary, deprecate primary after monitoring window. SDK helper startManagedRotation() will accept endpoints and timing parameters and expose status events for the host app.
- Ephemeral SSO: For enterprise customers using SAML/OIDC, provide a sample flow where the SDK exchanges a short-lived session token via a server-side BFF (for browser flows) or direct client credentials for server apps. Document the security trade-offs clearly.
- Streaming reauth: Use initial metadata/header for token + support a small control frame on the wire ("reauth_required") where the server indicates the token is about to expire; the SDK will pause the data stream, call AuthProvider.refresh(), and resume or reconnect with backoff. For transports that don't support control frames (plain HTTP chunked), fall back to 401-on-send detection with reconnection.
- Local dev ergonomics: Provide an auth-cli utility (or instructions) to mint ephemeral dev tokens wired to local secret stores (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Secret Service) and document fallback to dotenv files only for ephemeral local use.
- Telemetry: Emit anonymized events when tokens rotate, refresh failures, and streaming reconnects; tag events with customer ID for enterprise telemetry only with consent.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risks:
- UX friction if rotation helpers are too prescriptive; mitigation: make helpers opt-in and document recommended flows.
- Token leakage in examples: mitigation: remove any examples that show long-lived tokens in code snippets; recommend secret stores.
- Reauth race conditions during high-throughput streaming: mitigation: add jitter, ensure idempotent reconnects, and test at scale in staging.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement core auth primitives in SDK mono-repo (Python/JS/Go).
2) Add integration tests that simulate expiry and server control frames.
3) Publish docs + migration guide for existing customers.
4) Beta release to select customers (Dedicated + Private) for feedback.
5) Full release with security review sign-off and telemetry enabled.
